It first reads the containing sector to preserve bytes before the embedded block; other physical slots use header offset0 without a preliminary read. Read/write calls retry only result-1, up to ten attempts, and propagate remaining read failure or final write result. The function constructs and transforms the shared buffer but does not update x170/x270 itself; callers handle those maps.

facts.value: s32 (CardState* state): synchronously reconciles nine logical subfiles using the inclusive physical slot limit x460 and x170/x270 maps, while scheduling corrective CARD commands. Zero means no recorded error, not proof of full redundancy restoration: a missing duplicate with no negative/free slot is silently left unrepaired.

facts.rationale: Preserves exceptional shortages, mutation timing and error precedence.
facts.value: Rejects extent mismatch with-257. Selects complete sequence-consistent generations where available; missing blocks set-0x103, partial mixed generations-0x104. Modes1/2 negate nonselected mappings. Mode0 retains one secondary, queues disposal of extras, and queues source-read/destination-write pairs for missing or stale duplicates. Disposal failure sets-0x10B only if no earlier error, yet immediately invalidates that map entry regardless. Copy-submission failure sets-0x102 only over0/-0x10B. If no free destination exists, missing-copy repair is skipped without a new error. No local batch rollback or reservation of a newly chosen free destination occurs; map changes and accepted commands can survive a negative return.

facts.rationale: Corrects result-field confusion.
facts.value: Checkpoints the producer, enqueues type12 status inspection and type17 maintenance, and clears/rewinds appended commands if either admission fails. Queue rollback does not undo CARD work already executed.

facts.value: s32 (CardState* state, s32 file_index, u8* destination, s32 asynchronous, void (*callback)(s32,s32)). Block helpers skip copying when the supplied destination is null, but this is not a clear-only mode: the wrapper advances destination slices without a null guard, so arbitrary multi-block null-destination use is not established as safe.

facts.rationale: Documents nonterminal negative admission result and ignored substep rather than blanket transactional claims.
facts.value: Sync mode rejects busy1 with-264. Missing primary capacity returns-257; missing secondary capacity records-258 but continues. Complete matching copies return1 only synchronously; queued comparisons plus type6 gate later writes. Rewrites use (newest_sequence+1)&255; sync failures invalidate the affected map and return-260 for primary or-258 for secondary. Checked enqueue failures rewind the batch, but a preliminary physical-slot0 preservation-read enqueue is ignored. Queued setup publishes context type2 and releases the checkpoint even when returning pending-258, so a negative immediate result can coexist with queued work and a later callback. Terminal sync close returns-267 unless-258 already takes precedence.

facts.rationale: Qualifies copy-on-write claim with explicit in-place fallback.
facts.value: Verifies and updates one indexed logical payload, normally writing a new sequence into alternate/free physical slots and then retiring remaining old mappings. When alternate/free capacity is insufficient, it reuses current slots; therefore preserving a complete recoverable prior generation is not guaranteed. Supports synchronous execution and queued compare-before-write execution.

facts.rationale: Preserves subsystem mapping without overstating recoverability.
facts.value: Implements a generation-based update policy for Melee's HSD logical save components, with unchanged-data detection and preference for alternate-block replacement. Current blocks may be reused when spare capacity is insufficient, so its recovery properties are conditional rather than an unconditional copy-on-write guarantee.

facts.rationale: Preserves allocation-failure and ignored-admission exceptions.
facts.value: Sync mode rejects busy1 with-264 and opens the selected CARD file. Matching current data returns1 after close; otherwise excess alternates are cleared, then free slots and if needed current slots fill the replacement set. Insufficient capacity returns-257; in queued mode this path does not rewind earlier verification commands. Sequence advances modulo256. Checked enqueue failures rewind, but preliminary slot0 preservation-read admission is ignored. Sync writes update maps, invalidate failed destinations and negate remaining old mappings; queued completion publishes active context type3 rather than appending a terminal command. Successful sync close failure becomes-267.

facts.rationale: Makes exceptional early return part of the purpose contract.
facts.value: Recovery-oriented logical-payload updater: fills missing physical mappings from secondary/free slots, verifies the selected generation, and can dispose stale secondaries and rewrite a new sequence. The canonical synchronous path with any remaining secondary returns immediately after disposing its first secondary, even on success, before payload rewriting; the queued path schedules all remaining disposal and rewrite work.

evidence.why: Map and I/O data flow including early return.

facts.rationale: Corrects the previously unconditional disposal-to-rewrite flow.
facts.value: State geometry, x4C sizes and x170/x270 maps produce current, secondary and free-slot lists for the selected logical interval. Missing current slots are filled from secondary then free lists. Current slots and caller payload slices feed verification; remaining secondaries feed disposal. Queued mode proceeds to sequence-tagged writes and stores state/file-index/callback in context type4. Sync mode returns the first secondary-disposal result when any secondary remains; otherwise writes update maps and a final close precedes return.

facts.rationale: Corrects success-return interpretation.
facts.value: Effective s32 (CardState* state, s32 file_index, const void* payload, BOOL asynchronous, void (*callback)(s32 id,s32 result)); payload and callback are carried as s32 in the source ABI. Return1 denotes synchronous unchanged data; negative values report CARD/HSD/setup failures. Return0 can mean completed rewriting, successful queued setup, or only successful first-secondary disposal on the synchronous early-return branch; it does not always prove a completed payload update.

facts.rationale: Retains CARD recovery mapping while removing an unconditional completion guarantee.
facts.value: Implements recovery-oriented updates of HSD logical save components using surviving mappings, spare slots, content checks and sequence-tagged writes. This describes its role, not a guarantee of coherent replacement on every successful return: synchronous stale-secondary cleanup can return before rewriting the requested payload.

facts.rationale: Preserves the unusual successful early return and associated file lifetime.
facts.value: Sync mode rejects busy1 with-264; missing-map allocation exhausts secondary then free slots and returns-257 when insufficient. Matching data returns1 after close. Otherwise queued mode disposes all remaining secondaries then rewrites with sequence+1 modulo256. Sync mode instead disposes only the first remaining secondary, invalidates its map, closes only on negative disposal result, and returns that result unconditionally; successful disposal leaves the file open and skips rewriting. With no remaining secondary, sync rewriting updates or invalidates maps and final close failure becomes-267. Checked queued failures rewind, but preliminary slot0 preservation-read enqueue is ignored. Queued success publishes context type4 and releases checkpoint.

Logical application payload blocks are populated by a separate routine; snapshot-specific image serialization is not established here.

facts.rationale: Replaces rendered-name evidence with canonical component and lifetime tracing.

facts.value: initialize=0 enables comparison: synchronous match returns1, queued mode emits type10 comparisons followed by type6 gating. Queued initialization omits comparison and queues type4 clearing of the entire shared sector buffer before the final type9 write; noninitializing queued mode instead queues a type2 read with negative selector to preserve that sector without decoding it. Synchronous first-sector clear/read occurs only when x24+0x30<sector_size; subsequent clear/read uses the literal condition remaining+0x30<x24. Negative checked I/O/admission results return immediately; accepted prefix commands are not rolled back locally. CARD retry helpers retry only-1 up to ten attempts.

facts.rationale: Preserves first-slot exceptions, full-capacity source requirement and correct map direction.
facts.value: Processes file zero, later files1..8, shared spare region, then mode0 duplicate copies. Mode1 reserves the maximum full-file block count; mode2 ensures one spare; modes0/3 add no shared spare. Spare writes use logical ID0xFFFF. Nonnull payloads are read at full block capacity, including last blocks, rather than clamped to remaining file size. Checked errors stop without local queue rollback; preliminary slot0 read-enqueue errors are ignored. Sync slot0 tolerates-0x105 and does not record a success map update there; later success writes logical IDs into x170[physical_slot] and zero sequence, while failure invalidates the affected slot.

This is rollback of queue construction, not cancellation of executed I/O or rollback of output-buffer writes.

facts.rationale: Adds important exceptional result and output-lifetime behavior.
facts.value: CARD completion result and current command fields drive shared-buffer decoding, expected-content comparisons, optional copies, presentation digest checks and block-map updates. Most CARD/close failures enter hsd_804D7988, but type13 ignores close result and converts read/integrity/identifier failures solely into x170=-0x7FFF and x270=0. Type2 with negative selector stores the incoming arg1 (normally0 on that branch), not the negative close result. Type11 copies outputs before final digest mismatch can be detected. Accepted completion always clears command type and busy state and advances consumer modulo128, including unrecognized types that fall through the switch.

facts.rationale: Preserves numeric distinctions and exceptional branches instead of normalizing all failures.
facts.value: Returns without mutation unless shared mode is1. Types2/15 normally report decoding failure-0x105; comparison types5/10 report mismatch2; type11 reports trailing-digest mismatch-0x107 after optional output copies. Type2 negative selector skips decoding and, on failed close, assigns incoming arg1 rather than close error. Type13 always ignores close result and invalidates maps for failed read/validation without assigning shared result. Types1/16 update or invalidate written-slot maps; type7 copies the captured fileNo through a bounded loop that does not poll it; type8 reports status failure without closing. After any accepted switch path, command type becomes0, busy becomes0 and consumer advances modulo128.

facts.value: Retries CARDOpen only while result=-1, up to ten attempts, and propagates negative result. Its fileNo loop tests a captured tmp value rather than polling the field; captured negative fileNo returns the later loaded value without closing. Otherwise CARDClose is retried on-1 up to ten times and its final result is ignored. Ring admission rejects coincident producer/consumer with nonzero slot type using-265; success publishes request type5 with state, fileNo and callback, advances producer modulo32 and returns0. No interrupt masking is performed locally.
